args.summary: The payments-api v5.1.0 deploy (this morning) caused an 18% error rate across all production regions. Rolled back to the last known-healthy release, v5.0.0, in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west); rollout verified. Opening this incident to track root-cause investigation of the v5.1.0 regression and any residual customer impact during the degraded window.
args.title: payments-api v5.1.0 deploy causing elevated errors; rolled back to v5.0.0

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what I did:

1. **Identified the affected service** — the registry rejected "payments" but accepted **payments-api**, which was running v5.1.0 across all production regions, unhealthy with an 18% error rate.
2. **Found the last healthy release** — deployment history showed v5.0.0 (healthy) followed by v5.1.0 (degraded).
3. **Rolled back** payments-api to **v5.0.0** in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) — rollout verified.
4. **Opened SEV2 incident INC-0001** — "payments-api v5.1.0 deploy causing elevated errors; rolled back to v5.0.0" — the on-call engineer has been paged to investigate the root cause of the v5.1.0 regression.

Note: there was no customer impact window I could quantify from the incident tooling, so I left that for the on-call to assess. If you'd like, I can also deploy a fixed version later once v5.1.0's regression is resolved — that would just be a normal deploy of a known-good build.
